podcast.body: Written by Bill Danoff, co-writer of "Take Me Home, Country Roads," the song's title was inspired by a cafe menu item in 1974. Danoff developed the lyrics over about a year, pulling lines and metaphors from various sources, and the music was partly inspired by Rod Stewart's "Maggie May." Initially, the vocal blend of Bill Danoff and Taffy Nivert, joined by John Carroll and Margot Chapman, sounded "too straight," so legendary producer Phil Ramone and session musician Russell George were brought in to create the desired groove, incorporating a jazz background. It went to number one on July 10, 1976, the week after America's Bicentennial, becoming popular enough to name bowling leagues and racehorses, with children singing it without understanding its suggestive lyrics. "Afternoon delight went to number one on July 10th 1976 the week after America's bison teniel."
